paragraphs.english: Every morning, Ben crossed a bridge on his way to school. He usually looked at his phone while walking. One Tuesday, his phone battery was empty, so he watched the river instead. A small white bird stood near the water, and a worker was repairing a sign beside the path. Ben had never noticed either of them before. That afternoon, his art teacher asked students to draw something from their daily journey. Ben drew the bird, the bridge, and the worker's bright hat. His classmates were surprised because they used the same bridge but remembered only the busy road. For the next week, Ben put his phone in his bag during the walk. He saw how the river changed after rain and where flowers grew between stones. He still used his phone at other times. However, he learned that an ordinary journey could offer new things when he paid attention to the world around him.
paragraphs.translation: 毎朝、ベンは登校途中に橋を渡った。たいてい歩きながら携帯電話を見ていた。ある火曜日、携帯の電池が切れたので、代わりに川を見た。小さな白い鳥が水辺に立ち、作業員が道の横の標識を直していた。ベンは、それまでどちらにも気づいたことがなかった。その午後、美術の先生は日々の道中で見たものを描くよう生徒に頼んだ。ベンは鳥と橋、作業員の明るい色の帽子を描いた。級友は同じ橋を使っていたのに混んだ道路しか覚えておらず、驚いた。次の一週間、ベンは歩く間、携帯をかばんにしまった。雨の後に川がどう変わるかや、石の間のどこに花が育つかを見た。他の時間には、引き続き携帯を使った。しかし身の回りに注意を向ければ、ありふれた道中にも新たな発見があると学んだ。

paragraphs.english: A bakery near Emma's house became very popular after a local television program introduced it. On Saturdays, customers waited along a narrow street. People who needed to reach other shops found it difficult to pass. The baker wanted to serve everyone, but asking people to stand in a different line did not solve the problem. Emma suggested giving each customer a numbered card. A board by the door showed which numbers could enter. Customers could wait in the nearby square or visit another shop until their turn came. On the back of each card, Emma drew a small map of the square and marked a place to sit. The baker tested the system for two Saturdays. The street became easier to walk through, and several customers said they had discovered shops they had never visited. The bread did not change, but the way people waited improved the whole shopping area. Emma was pleased that her simple idea helped more than one business.
paragraphs.translation: 地元のテレビ番組で紹介され、エマの家の近くのパン屋はとても人気になった。土曜日には客が狭い通りに沿って待った。他の店へ行く必要のある人たちは、通り抜けにくいと感じた。店主は全員に販売したかったが、別の列へ並ばせるだけでは解決しなかった。エマは、客一人ずつに番号札を渡すことを提案した。入口の掲示板は、どの番号の人が入れるか示した。客は順番まで近くの広場で待ったり、別の店を訪ねたりできた。札の裏に、エマは広場の小さな地図を描き、座れる場所を示した。店主は二回の土曜日にその仕組みを試した。通りは歩きやすくなり、何人かの客は初めて行く店を発見したと言った。パンは変わらなかったが、待ち方が商店街全体をよくした。エマは、自分の簡単な案が複数の店に役立ちうれしかった。

paragraphs.english: For a history project, Tom found a map of his town from fifty years ago. It showed a long road through the center and a lake beside the old station. Tom could still see the road, but he could not find the lake anywhere. He thought the map was wrong. His aunt suggested looking at old photographs in the town office. In one photograph, people were skating on the lake. Another showed workers filling part of it with earth. A town report explained that homes and a new station had later been built there. Tom visited the area again. A short street was still called Lake Road, although no water could be seen. He added photographs and a modern map to his project. Comparing them helped him understand that a familiar town had a history hidden under its present buildings. He also learned to look for more evidence before deciding that an old document was mistaken.
paragraphs.translation: 歴史の課題で、トムは五十年前の町の地図を見つけた。中心を通る長い道と、旧駅の横の湖が載っていた。道は今も見えたが、湖はどこにも見つからなかった。地図が間違っていると思った。叔母は町役場で古い写真を見ることを勧めた。一枚の写真では、人々が湖の上でスケートをしていた。別の一枚は、作業員が湖の一部を土で埋める様子を示していた。町の報告書には、後に住宅と新駅がそこに建てられたとあった。トムは再びその地区を訪ねた。水は見えないのに、短い通りが今もレイク通りと呼ばれていた。課題に写真と現代の地図を追加した。比べることで、見慣れた町にも現在の建物の下に隠れた歴史があると理解できた。古い文書が間違いだと決める前に、さらに証拠を探すことも学んだ。

paragraphs.english: When the school bought new chairs, a teacher asked students what to do with the old ones. Some were broken, but many were still strong. Mark suggested sending them all to a recycling center. His friend Nina thought they should first ask whether anyone could use them. The class contacted a children's theater group that practiced in an empty hall. The group needed seats for its audience but could not afford new ones. Students cleaned the strong chairs and checked them with the school caretaker. They sent only the safe ones to the theater. Broken parts went to the recycling center separately. At the first performance, the students sat on chairs they had used for years. The theater leader thanked them for making the hall more welcoming. Mark realized that recycling was useful, but finding a new use for a whole object could sometimes be a better first step. The class began keeping a list of other things people might need.
paragraphs.translation: 学校が新しい椅子を買うと、先生は古い椅子をどうするか生徒に尋ねた。壊れた椅子もあったが、多くはまだ丈夫だった。マークは全部をリサイクル施設へ送ろうと提案した。友人ニナは、先に誰か使える人がいないか尋ねるべきだと考えた。クラスは、空いたホールで練習する子供の劇団に連絡した。劇団は観客席が必要だったが、新品を買う余裕がなかった。生徒は丈夫な椅子を掃除し、学校の管理担当者と確認した。安全なものだけを劇場へ送った。壊れた部品は別にリサイクル施設へ送った。最初の公演で、生徒は何年も使っていた椅子に座った。劇団代表は、ホールをより歓迎される雰囲気にしたことに感謝した。リサイクルも役立つが、物全体の新しい使い道を探す方が、時には最初の手順としてよいとマークは気づいた。クラスは、他に人が必要としそうな物の一覧を作り始めた。

paragraphs.english: Lucy loved buying beautiful notebooks. She had five at home, but most pages were empty. She wanted each notebook to contain perfect writing and neat pictures. Whenever she made a spelling mistake on the first page, she stopped using that notebook. One day, her older brother showed her a notebook from his first year at college. It contained crossed-out words, arrows, rough drawings, and questions without answers. He explained that it helped him work through difficult ideas. A notebook did not have to be a finished book for other people to admire. Lucy chose one of her empty notebooks and wrote a plan for a school play. When a scene did not work, she crossed it out and tried another. A month later, the pages looked messy, but her play was ready. She felt more proud of that used notebook than of the clean ones on her shelf. Mistakes had become signs of progress rather than reasons to stop.
paragraphs.translation: ルーシーは美しいノートを買うのが大好きだった。家に五冊あったが、ほとんどのページは空白だった。各ノートには完璧な文章と整った絵を入れたかった。最初のページでつづりを間違えるたび、そのノートを使うのをやめた。ある日、兄は大学一年の時のノートを見せた。そこには消した単語、矢印、粗い下絵、未解決の問いがあった。難しい考えをじっくり整理するのに役立つと兄は説明した。ノートは、人に感心してもらうための完成した本でなくてもよかった。ルーシーは空白のノートの一冊を選び、学校の劇の案を書いた。ある場面がうまくいかないと、線で消して別の案を試した。一か月後、ページは雑然としていたが、劇は完成していた。棚のきれいなノートより、その使い込んだノートを誇らしく思った。間違いは、やめる理由ではなく進歩の印になっていた。

content.selectionReason: 高校入試相当を目安とする150〜250語の独自長文。各形式10題。難易度・自然さ・解答一意性は校閲待ち。

previousSyntax.sentence: Lucy chose one of her empty notebooks and wrote a plan for a school play.
previousSyntax.translation: ルーシーは空のノートを一冊選び学校劇の案を書いた。
previousSyntax.explanation: 同じ主語Lucyに過去形choseとwroteがandで並ぶ。

sentences.english: Lucy loved buying beautiful notebooks.
sentences.translation: ルーシーは美しいノートを買うのが大好きだった。
sentences.sourceEnglish: Lucy loved buying beautiful notebooks.

sentences.english: She had five at home, but most pages were empty.
sentences.translation: 家に五冊あったが、ほとんどのページは空白だった。
sentences.sourceEnglish: She had five at home, but most pages were empty.

sentences.english: She wanted each notebook to contain perfect writing and neat pictures.
sentences.translation: 各ノートには完璧な文章と整った絵を入れたかった。
sentences.sourceEnglish: She wanted each notebook to contain perfect writing and neat pictures.

sentences.english: Whenever she made a spelling mistake on the first page, she stopped using that notebook.
sentences.translation: 最初のページでつづりを間違えるたび、そのノートを使うのをやめた。
sentences.sourceEnglish: Whenever she made a spelling mistake on the first page, she stopped using that notebook.

sentences.english: One day, her older brother showed her a notebook from his first year at college.
sentences.translation: ある日、兄は大学一年の時のノートを見せた。
sentences.sourceEnglish: One day, her older brother showed her a notebook from his first year at college.

sentences.english: It contained crossed-out words, arrows, rough drawings, and questions without answers.
sentences.translation: そこには消した単語、矢印、粗い下絵、未解決の問いがあった。
sentences.sourceEnglish: It contained crossed-out words, arrows, rough drawings, and questions without answers.

sentences.english: He explained that it helped him work through difficult ideas.
sentences.translation: 難しい考えをじっくり整理するのに役立つと兄は説明した。
sentences.sourceEnglish: He explained that it helped him work through difficult ideas.

sentences.english: A notebook did not have to be a finished book for other people to admire.
sentences.translation: ノートは、人に感心してもらうための完成した本でなくてもよかった。
sentences.sourceEnglish: A notebook did not have to be a finished book for other people to admire.

sentences.english: Lucy chose one of her empty notebooks and wrote a plan for a school play.
sentences.translation: ルーシーは空白のノートの一冊を選び、学校の劇の案を書いた。
sentences.sourceEnglish: Lucy chose one of her empty notebooks and wrote a plan for a school play.

sentences.english: When a scene did not work, she crossed it out and tried another.
sentences.translation: ある場面がうまくいかないと、線で消して別の案を試した。
sentences.sourceEnglish: When a scene did not work, she crossed it out and tried another.

sentences.english: A month later, the pages looked messy, but her play was ready.
sentences.translation: 一か月後、ページは雑然としていたが、劇は完成していた。
sentences.sourceEnglish: A month later, the pages looked messy, but her play was ready.

sentences.english: She felt more proud of that used notebook than of the clean ones on her shelf.
sentences.translation: 棚のきれいなノートより、その使い込んだノートを誇らしく思った。
sentences.sourceEnglish: She felt more proud of that used notebook than of the clean ones on her shelf.

sentences.english: Mistakes had become signs of progress rather than reasons to stop.
sentences.translation: 間違いは、やめる理由ではなく進歩の印になっていた。
sentences.sourceEnglish: Mistakes had become signs of progress rather than reasons to stop.

exerciseParagraphs.english: Lucy loved buying beautiful notebooks. She had five at home, but most pages were empty. She wanted each notebook to contain perfect writing and neat pictures. Whenever she made a spelling mistake on the first page, she stopped using that notebook.
exerciseParagraphs.translation: ルーシーは美しいノートを買うのが大好きだった。家に五冊あったが、ほとんどのページは空白だった。各ノートには完璧な文章と整った絵を入れたかった。最初のページでつづりを間違えるたび、そのノートを使うのをやめた。

exerciseParagraphs.english: One day, her older brother showed her a notebook from his first year at college. It contained crossed-out words, arrows, rough drawings, and questions without answers. He explained that it helped him work through difficult ideas. A notebook did not have to be a finished book for other people to admire.
exerciseParagraphs.translation: ある日、兄は大学一年の時のノートを見せた。そこには消した単語、矢印、粗い下絵、未解決の問いがあった。難しい考えをじっくり整理するのに役立つと兄は説明した。ノートは、人に感心してもらうための完成した本でなくてもよかった。

exerciseParagraphs.english: Lucy chose one of her empty notebooks and wrote a plan for a school play. When a scene did not work, she crossed it out and tried another. A month later, the pages looked messy, but her play was ready. She felt more proud of that used notebook than of the clean ones on her shelf. Mistakes had become signs of progress rather than reasons to stop.
exerciseParagraphs.translation: ルーシーは空白のノートの一冊を選び、学校の劇の案を書いた。ある場面がうまくいかないと、線で消して別の案を試した。一か月後、ページは雑然としていたが、劇は完成していた。棚のきれいなノートより、その使い込んだノートを誇らしく思った。間違いは、やめる理由ではなく進歩の印になっていた。
